reasoning: A hybrid strategy is chosen to combine autonomous reasoning with rigorous external explainability tools to ensure robust identification of shared spurious features. Autonomous analysis helps identify obvious commonalities in the input data, while XAI tools provide quantitative attribution scores to validate which features have high influence despite lacking semantic relevance. This combination enhances both precision and depth in detecting spurious patterns.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify the set of features that appear in both instance 13590 and instance 14465, and evaluate if any feature is consistently present across all misclassified instances (even if not explicitly listed)
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across the two instances and a note on whether these features are common across all misclassified instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Assess whether the shared features (e.g., education-num=9, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse) have plausible spurious correlations with the target class, especially given that these features are common in both instances and seem semantically unrelated to income prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: An interpretation of whether the shared features are likely spurious due to coincidental patterns or overfitting to population-level trends

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP is selected for its ability to provide calibrated, interpretable feature importance across instances, especially in identifying features with high attribution despite semantic irrelevance. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer complementary local and global attribution, helping detect spurious signals. Sensitivity analysis quantifies the feature impact, confirming whether setting a shared feature to zero changes the prediction significantly—indicating spuriousness. Together, these tools validate shared, high-attribution features that do not logically correlate with the target class.
